digest.component_or_area: Event-derivation readers over durable ticket event store
propositions: Read-only derivations of agent-process metrics from raw event files (sorted chronologically, including compaction-retired events, excluding snapshots) and compiled terminal state using existing reducer helpers, where per-event or multi-occurrence data (attempts, rework windows, reopen counts) requires raw event files and single-value terminal facts (first-pass rate via last_reopened_at absence, revert recovery via reverts[]) use compiled state from reduce_ticket.

Distinct claim sessions (open→in_progress STATUS edges with distinct data.session values) counted via raw event files yield attempts_per_ticket; first_pass_rate is the fraction of closed tickets in range with no last_reopened_at terminal value; rework_within_days(n) counts closed→open→closed transitions within n calendar days measured from raw STATUS event timestamps.

Reopen_recovery counts all tickets with ≥1 closed→open STATUS edge in range (raw scan required for complete edge count); revert_recovery counts tickets whose state[reverts] contains a revert targeting STATUS or COMMITS event type, filtering out substantive-reverts from COMMENT/LINK events.

Metrics return None (→Unavailable) over empty date ranges and return 0 (measured zero) for populated ranges with no qualifying events; all metrics register with source='structural' and confidence='high' (authoritative, HLC filename timestamps are exact wall-clock nanoseconds).

Unit tests verify two distinct open→in_progress sessions yield attempts_per_ticket==2; closed→open→closed 3 days apart counts in rework_within_days(7) but not 10 days apart; first_pass_rate excludes ever-reopened tickets; revert_recovery counts STATUS-targeted reverts but not COMMENT-targeted reverts; retired events are included.

Metrics are implemented as read-only functions taking (repo_root, since, until) in src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py registered into src/rebar/metrics/registry.py; no new event emission occurs and metrics reuse existing reducer sort/filter/resolution helpers rather than reinventing file-listing or event-handling logic.
